seo_title: Cost of Living in Kathmandu 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Kathmandu per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Nepal in a valley at the foot of the Himalayas: visa on arrival, very low prices, ancient temples and mountains nearby. The downsides are basic infrastructure, power outages and air quality.
pros: Visa on arrival for Russian citizens
Ancient temples and an old-town atmosphere
Friendly people and a calm pace of life

visa_steps.title: Visa on arrival
visa_steps.description: Russians get the visa at the airport (for 15, 30 or 90 days).

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Apartments and houses are rented by the month very cheaply.

visa_steps.title: SIM card and money
visa_steps.description: A local SIM card is cheap; you'll need rupees in cash and a foreign bank card.

visa_steps.title: Long-term stay

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Kathmandu?
faq.answer: A visa is issued on arrival for 15, 30 or 90 days, with the option to extend.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Kathmandu?
faq.answer: Very cheap — one of the most budget-friendly options in Asia. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Kathmandu?
faq.answer: Nepali; English is widely used in tourism.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Kathmandu?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You need rupees in cash and a foreign bank card.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Kathmandu?
faq.answer: Mild in the valley: warm summers with a monsoon and cool, dry winters.

faq.question: Why move to Kathmandu?
faq.answer: Low prices, a spiritual atmosphere and proximity to the Himalayas — the main base for trekking in Nepal.

reviews.text: Kathmandu means dirt-cheap prices, temples and the Himalayas right there. The downsides are weak infrastructure, power cuts and dust, and the internet sometimes lets you down.
I stayed for the atmosphere and the mountains. People are kind and life is cheap. There's plenty of day-to-day hassle, but spiritually and naturally this is a special place.
